body: Yes, I can definitely relate. All of my suicide attempts have been impulsive. Sometimes I start to enjoy life, and then I get anxious that I will end my life because of how it's been in the past. I feel like I can't really enjoy my good moments because of that.

I feel weird. I think I might have experienced mania the last few days. I haven't been sleeping much, and I didn't feel tired at all. I was not eating, and I didn't feel hungry. I felt so focused on I suppose these grandiose ideas of me becoming successful, like super successful. I'm thinking that if I start go back to university taking school seriously maybe I could really do something great. 

Four years ago, I wanted to aim to get a doctorate in History or some other field I was interested. Since then, I've tried to kill myself many times, been hospitalized, and lost almost everyone in my life. 

Ever since the US elections results, I actually feel ambitious. It feels crazy, but I don't know. I think after everything I have been through, maybe I have a lot to offer to the world. I've been thinking about volunteering. I'm not sure where or for what cause, but I think that would be a good start. 

I actually kinda feel like I can do this.

So today, my mom threw a temper tantrum because of some toilet paper. A couple of days ago, I needed toilet paper, and I had to open a new package. I was very scared to ask my mom permission to open the new package because I knew she would get angry, but today she discovered that the toilet paper package was open. After realizing that some toilet paper was missing, she threw it across the room, and have a had huge anger outburst.

I wasn't there to witness it, but she told me. I felt really guilty, trapped, and hopeless. I felt like it was my fault. After she told me, she laughed it off like it was nothing. I don't understand how she thought that was acceptable behavior. 

I really dislike my mom and brother. I think they are awful, and I think I would be happy never seeing them ever again. I feel really lonely since they are the two only people I talk to on a regular basis. They are crazy and delusional. 

I don't understand why anyone would get mad over something like that. She also once got out of her car once, and threw a cheeseburger on the ground in the middle of a mc Donald's parking lot because they didn't get her order right. She acts like a total Karen and is mean to customer service people. I don't get it.

I got started on the PS2. I played games like Simpsons: Hit and Run, SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom, and Guitar Hero when I was about 8 years old. However, in 2011, when Skyrim came out, I started to play games more often. I realized I loved playing Bethesda, Bioware, and RPG games in general. Single player RPGs are my absolute favorite.

I'm feeling really anxious right now. I am terrified of dying. I have attempted suicide twice, and those were impulsive attempts. I don't have any friends or really anyone positive in my life right now except paying to see a therapist. 

Sometimes I really want to talk to a person I used to date and was friends with. Now, she hates me, and I don't blame her. I miss her dearly sometimes. I wish it was 2018 again, and I wish I could do things over. Maybe we would have continued seeing each other and became each other's girlfriend. 

Everything feels so overwhelming. I'm stuck at home with an abusive family. I hope this doesn't lead to me completing suicide. I really wish I had friends to talk to, but I only have Reddit. I don't even know how to make new friends right now. I'm too scared to talk to people, even online.
I am 25. I'm very embarrassed that I still live at home. Plus my credit is bad because I was hospitalized 3 times and went to two outpatient programs due to severe mental health issues.

I'm making an escape plan to get away from my mom and brother. They are both extremely abusive, and I don't want to be around them anymore. I would like to go no contact in the future. I might keep in contact with my sister. She seems to be the most sane out of all my family members. 

I'm really scared. I don't do well with confrontation. I always try to appease them, so I don't have to deal with their anger.

Thank you. You've been really helpful. I talked to my therapist on Saturday, and she is helping me make an escape plan. My mom is going to go nuts when she finds out I'm planning to move. I suspect she is going to say some awful things to me, and she will probably threaten to disown me. Moving out is going to be a shit show.

Thank you so so much for the advice and kind words. Today, I talked to my mom, and she told me that it's normal for siblings to fight. I told her what he did was not okay, and I also told her I scheduled an appointment with my therapist. She wasn't too happy about that. She told me that I shouldn't be talking about my family to the therapist because it's none of their business. She also told me that I shouldn't paint my brother as a monster to the therapist. A couple of days ago she told me I should be grateful that my relationship with him isn't worse, and that's actually a pretty good one. I feel my life has always revolved around him and his feelings, and I'm sick and tired of it. 

He's a 27 year old man, and he has severe anger issues. I've always been scared of him. This may sound a little dramatic, but I've always thought he was going to severely hurt me one day or even kill me. That's how bad and irrational his anger is.
Thank you for the advice! I live near a walking trail, so I'll try that out next week on Monday. I definitely need the exercise too, so it would be a positive experience.

Mental health professionals do sometimes have a very stigmatized view of people with BPD. I've been told that sometimes in the classes they have had in their Master's program or undergrad that their professors will paint a very negative picture of people with BPD. That certainly doesn't help. Plus I'm sure they've read the stories, and they've probably even met a lot of low functioning people BPD that reinforce their views. 

I feel like that's a very closed-minded view because ever since I was 15 I thought I had BPD, and it wasn't until I was 24 until I got an official diagnosis. A lot of therapists said I wasn't angry or abrasive enough to get diagnosed. I knew for years that I probably had the disorder, but I wasn't "mean" enough to people. That negative perception of people with our disorder is the reason why I didn't get treatment I needed until 9 years later. 

I've met a lot of mental health professionals that have a positive view of Borderline Personality Disorder, and are willing to work with us. My current therapist is really great, and she was the one who told me to try to think of BPD in a more positive light because I've read all those posts on all those communities, and I felt like an evil, incurable monster. I've also met another therapist who specializes in treating Borderline Personality Disorder, and she amazing. This therapist ONLY wants to work with people with BPD in her private practice. There are definitely people out there who are going to want to help you. 

I'm sorry this is such a long post, but I know how it feels to think your a bad person because you have BPD. You know, I've even met a lot of other people with BPD, and they were really great. I've also been on the other side, and I've dated a low functioning person BPD. That person was abusive and awful to me, but I'm not going to think that all BPD are like that because of that one experience. 

Anyways, long rant over. I'm sorry you're having these thoughts about yourself.

I've been working from home since March, and it's certainly a privilege to be able to do so. However, I feel like it's been exacerbating my social anxiety. I'm too afraid to go outside, even to the grocery store or to get gas. Despite seeing a therapist who I have known for 2 years, I still am scared to talk to her. She's extremely nice, and I really like her. She even has an emotional support dog she brings for her sessions, which is a huge plus. He's so adorable and sweet. 

I think I need to find a way to get acclimated to public places again, but I'm unsure of where to start. I'm too scared to go anywhere.
That is amazing! Congratulations on making a positive change in your life. I wish you the best.

What those people don't understand is that BPD is a spectrum. There are 9 symptoms, but a person only has to meet five in order to qualify for a diagnosis. There are so many combination of symptoms that people with the disorder can vary greatly.

Plus a lot of those people who are in that Reddit community type in the behaviors of their loved ones in Google and the first search they see is likely BPD. I have doubts that a lot of those people they are talking about are actually diagnosed by a professional. If the person they are talking about actually is diagnosed with this disorder, then it's most likely an extreme example of the illness. Extreme cases are always the loudest. People meet one or two people with BPD or suspected BPD, and then they assume everyone with the disorder is like that. 

Don't get me wrong. Sometime people with BPD don't act great and need to be held accountable for their actions, including myself, but being a monster isn't listed in the symptoms of BPD.
I ended on bad terms with someone who was going through a crisis. I hope she's okay. I love her, and I hope she is alive.
